meta.description: Heuristic-layer anchors: callee params whose every observed call-site argument is an immediate constant -> int-family type set. Immediates were dropped by the IDA extractor ("立即数只占槽位，不产边" in ida_extract.py::_scan_call_args); this file reconstructs them by Capstone-disassembling the exact IDA-input binary (sha256-verified) with the extractor's exact backward-scan semantics: stop at call/ret/retn/j*, cap 32 insns, window bounded by function start, scan-order push i == param{i} (no CC offset, mirroring _assign_push_params and the existing P:fn:k entity space).

binary.identity: IDA-input binary per full_export v3 provenance

meta.all_const_criterion: >=1 plain-numeric immediate observation AND 0 non-immediate push observations (register/memory/address-valued immediate) AND 0 existing CALL_ARG edges for (callee,paramK) — existing edges are non-immediate by construction and also cover sites our scan cannot see (incl. vtable-resolved call sites); address-valued immediates (push offset global / function address) count as POINTER evidence and disqualify
caveats: heuristic layer — "param only ever passed constants" is int-family evidence, not a proof; const 0/1 may also be pointer NULL / flag bits

address-valued immediates (values inside any image section VA range) are treated as pointer arguments and disqualify — they encode push offset global/string/function-address, which the IDA-side extractor resolves to symbol sources rather than dropping
paramK numbering mirrors the extractor convention (nearest push = param0, no fastcall ecx/edx offset) for consistency with existing P:fn:k entities
tail jmp-to-function sites are included as observations (real call sites the original extractor does not scan)
call sites with callee not at a known function start are skipped (mid-function / thunk-into-middle targets)
